newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast prods up with NYMEX, supply concerns.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast prods up with NYMEX, supply concerns.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot gasoline prices edged higher Friday in line with a stronger NYMEX futures market and lingering rumors of a diesel-making problem at Arco's Los Angeles refiner, traders said.
ARCO earlier denied the rumors of a problem at its 265,000 barrel-per-day refinery at Carson, Calif..
But traders said the plant's 43,000 barrel-per-day hydrocracker might be off line, based on a price hike at the companies truck loading terminals.
The rumor, combined with a 1.4 million drop of gasoline supply last week sent gasoline and diesel higher Friday.
Meanwhile, support came from futures markets, where NYMEX heating oil for April rose 1.11 cents to 55.33 cents a gallon. Front-month gasoline firmed 1.54 cents to 65.77 cents.

"The Merc (New York Mercantile Exchange) is up and none of the turnarounds are over," a trader said, referring to ongoing planned repairs at Mobil's Los Angeles refinery and Exxon's facility near San Francisco.
Wholesale bids for low sulphur diesel in Los Angeles rose one cent from Thursday to 64 cents, while offers edged 0.50 cents higher to 64.50 cents.
L.A. CARB unleaded gasoline rose 0.50 cents to 77.50/78.50 cents. San Francisco grade stood about four cents lower at 73.50/75 cents.
